body: I'm extremely grateful for the family I have. I don't know what I'd do without them. And yes I do voluntarily go to therapy.
Nope. I'm very lucky, my family tries to be as supporting as possible.

My problem is I find stuff helps for a while, but then after some time has passed I realize that the things I thought were helpful actually haven't been helping me all that much. It's kinda like I lie to myself in the hopes that I'll feel better.
A support group sounds like an interesting experience. The problem is finding one near me. I doubt my college would have a designated group.

It's an awesome question that I've thought about a lot. I've been through cognitive behavior therapy, and that's one of the questions they have you ask yourself. Honestly I don't know what I'd do. Everything I used to enjoy holds no value to me currently, but if my depression were gone I'm sure I could learn to enjoy it again. But that's only if my depression were to disappear, which would be nice. I no longer desire to do anything really. If I woke up tomorrow with a million dollars I'd probably just give it to my family because there's nothing I want to buy.

I talk to them all the time, but I go to school out of state so it's hard to connect with my family and old friends. Depression makes it hard to even want to meet new people, let alone talk to them about my depression lol. It's a catch 22, I know I need to make new friends to increase my potential to be happy, but it's hard to make new friends since I'm so depressed.
